facts.situation: James and Caroline Whitmore are joint clients. James completed the sale of his business in April; the transition has been busy and emotional for both. The £850,000 completion payment is held in a solicitor's client account, with £200,000 already committed to repaying a bridging loan due shortly. A deferred earnout of up to £400,000 is payable over the next two years subject to business revenue targets; none has been received and it is not guaranteed. Their objectives are long-term growth and a tax-efficient investment base capable of replacing James's income when he steps back from full-time work in about three years. They currently require no portfolio income. Possible consultancy work is unsettled. The agreed risk profile is 4, balanced to moderate. James is concerned about exceeding pension contribution limits. Future help with grandchildren's school fees and a possible charitable donation are aspirations only, with no action intended in this report.

actions.action: Repay the bridging loan from the completion proceeds before investing the available proceeds.
Top up James's Holloway ISA, H4-ISA-J, using his allowance for the new tax year.
Top up Caroline's Holloway ISA, H4-ISA-C, using her allowance for the new tax year.
Contribute to James's Brightwell SIPP, B4-SIPP-J, at an appropriate level within applicable limits.
Contribute to Caroline's Brightwell SIPP, B4-SIPP-C, at an appropriate level within applicable limits.
Add completion proceeds to the Holloway joint GIA, H4-GIA-HJ.
Sell part of the existing investments in the Holloway joint GIA, H4-GIA-HJ, and rebalance it.
Invest the remaining available proceeds in a new jointly held investment account, which does not yet exist in the client database.
Leave the Meridian offshore bond, M4-BOND-J, unchanged for now and revisit at the next review.
